verdict: Nike's revenue was flat at $12.4B, and although gross margin widened to 44.8%, higher brand marketing and overhead spending pulled net income down 5% to $1.2B.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — footwear rose 4%, apparel fell 1%, and equipment jumped 17%.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Nike's second-biggest region — footwear fell 3%, apparel fell 9%, equipment rose 30%.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Footwear rose 5%, apparel fell 4% and equipment rose 17%.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Chuck Taylor brand — revenue fell 19% on declines in North America and Western Europe.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global Brand Divisions revenue of $9M plus Corporate of -$14M, mostly currency-hedge results — a small negative this quarter.

opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and brand marketing — higher brand marketing and Olympic-related spending.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Running the company — wages, distribution centers and administration.

otherDetail: $52M of net interest income, plus $16M of other income, net.
footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($9M) and Corporate (-$14M, mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.

takeaways.title: Revenue flat, regions split
takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $12,429M: Greater China grew 5%, North America and Asia Pacific & Latin America 3% each, while Europe, Middle East & Africa fell 3% and Converse dropped 19%.

takeaways.title: Margin widened, spending rose faster
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 150 basis points to 44.8% on strategic pricing and lower freight and logistics costs — but demand creation spending rose 10% and operating overhead 6%, so operating income fell.

takeaways.title: Profit eased against a strong comparison
takeaways.text: Net income fell 5% to $1,172M and EPS 3% to $0.77. Inventories fell 13% year over year to $7.7B as Nike cleared the prior year's excess stock.
